description: Build your dream mountain home on this exceptional southwest-facing homesite in Couch Mountain, where long-range mountain views, abundant natural light, and spectacular sunsets create an unforgettable setting. This private lot backs up to conserved land and is framed by mature hardwoods, offering both beauty and lasting privacy. Three unique rock formations provide opportunities to create a distinctive driveway entrance, landscape feature, or architectural focal point. Additionally, several attractive boulders near the front of the property were intentionally placed there for future landscaping and garden design. Inspired by traditional Japanese garden "rock setting" techniques, these stones were selected and relocated to the site rather than naturally emerging from the ground. The lot has already been cleared for site work, soil testing is complete, and it is approved for a 4-bedroom septic system. A gentle slope offers flexibility for a walkout basement, crawl space, or single-level home design. A builder has performed an initial evaluation in 6 excavated test pits in the proposed building envelope and determined that surface rock was removed without the need for drilling. A 2-foot topographic survey is available, and underground power is already in place. Chickens and bees are permitted. Residents enjoy access to a 138-acre nature preserve, private hiking trails, a mountaintop park, community gardens, greenhouse, vegetable stand, and apiaries. Conveniently located between Asheville and Hendersonville, you'll enjoy easy access to dining, outdoor recreation, and everything Western North Carolina has to offer. A rare opportunity to build in a mountain community that blends natural beauty, privacy, and connection to the land.

description: It's been a year since we settled in and my back deck has slowly become my favorite room in the house. My three-bedroom home is nothing showy around 1400 sq.ft., but the walk out basement is full of light, and we love to spend the cool evenings on the back porch. Most mornings I'm out on the upstairs porch off the main living room, coffee growing cold, just watching the stream catch the light. The stream’s constant murmur sold me on this lot before we’d graded the house seat. At 2,400 feet, the hardwoods hold onto a coolness the valley below doesn't get, and I trimmed the rhododendron along the bank so I could see our many visitors. I've learned the creek's morning rhythm. Most mornings I’ll see a doe and her fawn pick their way along the far bank. Wild turkeys work the leaf litter past the tree line. Chipmunks scold me from the rock pile, while the songbirds and Carolina wrens fill the air with song. The occasional pileated woodpecker hammering somewhere up the ridge never really stops. It's the kind of quiet during the day that's full, not empty. At night, it's the other kind of quiet. No streetlights, no traffic, with only two homes above my end of the road means the only thing passing by after dark is the occasional set of headlights pulling into a driveway I recognize. Crickets and katydids take over from the birds, an owl calls from somewhere across the stream, and the stars do what they can't do in town. And yet I'm not alone out here, my neighbors in Pinnacle Mountain View are close enough that someone notices if my lights are off too many nights in a row, close enough to call when a tree comes down across the publicly maintained road. Privacy and community, somehow, in the same acre of woods. On weekends I'm at DuPont or Pisgah admiring the waterfalls, miles of trail, with more biking than I'll ever get through. description: This 101 acre farm offers a combination of productive agricultural land, quality hunting habitat, and excellent accessibility in Cleveland County, North Carolina. With a combination of fenced pasture, tillable ground, and mixed timber, the property is well-suited for livestock, farming, recreation, or investment. Designed for cattle production, the farm features multiple fenced pastures with quality tensile fencing, multiple gated entry points, automatic cattle waterers, and two well-maintained metal pole barns that provide ample storage for equipment, hay, or livestock operations. The level to rolling topography is highly usable, making all parts of the property easy to manage and access. A small creek flows through the wooded portion of the property, providing natural habitat and protection for wildlife. The property has an excellent history of whitetail management and successful harvests, making it equally appealing to hunters and outdoor enthusiasts. With approximately 900 feet of frontage along Sandy Run Church Road and multiple access points, the property offers convenient entry for agricultural equipment and recreational use. This is a private, rural setting that buyers seem to look for; however, it is just a short distance from Highway 74 and the South Carolina state line. Nearby towns include Shelby, Boiling Springs, Rutherfordton, and Forest City. A 1971 brick home is located on the property and is being given no contributory value; however, this may be a fixer-upper opportunity for some buyers or an excellent location to build a new home with utilities in place. Whether you're looking to expand a cattle operation, establish a working farm, create a premier hunting property, start homesteading, or invest in a versatile tract of land, this Cleveland County farm offers the acreage, infrastructure, and location to make it a standout opportunity.

Various age classes of loblolly pine stands, large sections of mature hardwoods, and eleven food plots make up the balance of the property, and the timber stands include an abundance of truly massive specimens of sawtimber pine and oak trees. description: Exchange is a historic waterfront plantation situated in the prestigious Plantersville District of Georgetown County on the banks of the Pee Dee River. The property traces its roots to a 1735 Land Grant from King George II.  Neighboring plantations include Chicora Wood, Breakwater, Rosebank, Hasty Point, Glenmore and Arundel. At its peak in the 1840s this area was producing 50% of the rice exported from America and coastal Georgetown became one of the wealthiest cities in America.,Today, Exchange is known for its hunting, fishing and exceptional beauty. There are open pine woodlands, hardwood forests, clover fields, bass ponds and waterfowl impoundments providing habitat for deer, turkeys, doves and especially all types of ducks. The house and grounds are stunning. The main house and rice barn are on the National Historic Registry.,Exchange has been in the same family for over 80 years. The property is protected by a conservation easement with Wetlands America Trust / Ducks Unlimited.

description: The Norton Farm North offers 30.39+/- acres of productive farmland and woods in the Green Sea area of Horry County, South Carolina. With nearly an even split between cultivated ground and timber, this is the kind of traditional Carolina farm that can serve several purposes for its future owner. Approximately 18+/- acres are currently planted in soybeans, providing immediate agricultural use along with an attractive setting across the open fields. The balance consists of roughly 12+/- acres of wooded land, giving the property a good mix of cover, habitat, and privacy. The transition between the fields and woods creates natural travel corridors and feeding areas for wildlife, with hunting opportunities for whitetail deer, wild turkey, and upland game. The farm has frontage along county-maintained Norton Road, providing convenient year-round access. With no HOA or building restrictions currently in place, a future owner has the flexibility to continue farming the property, establish pasture, build a country home, create a recreational retreat, or simply hold the land as a long-term investment. One of this farms strongest attributes is its location. It sits just 2 miles from Green Sea-Floyds High School and less than 15 minutes from either Loris, SC or Tabor City, NC. Conway, Longs, and Whiteville, NC are all approximately 30 minutes away, while North Myrtle Beach and Lake Waccamaw, NC can be reached in roughly 45 minutes. The Norton Farm North combines productive acreage, wooded habitat, road frontage, and a quiet rural setting while remaining within an easy drive of communities throughout northeastern South Carolina and southeastern North Carolina. For buyers looking for a manageable Horry County farm with agricultural, recreational, and homesite potential, this 30.39+/- acre property deserves a closer look.

description: Just outside the Conway city limits, this 14.99+/- acre property offers a combination that is becoming increasingly difficult to find in Horry County: manageable acreage, road frontage, freedom from an HOA, and convenient access to both town and some of the regions best-known rivers and outdoor destinations. There are currently no HOA or building restrictions in place, leaving the property with fewer limitations than are commonly found closer to the rapidly growing Conway and Myrtle Beach areas. Located only approximately 1.5 miles from the Conway city limits, the property provides the feel and flexibility of acreage outside town while keeping shopping, dining, schools, medical facilities, and other everyday conveniences within easy reach. One of the propertys strongest attributes is its location within the river country of Horry and Georgetown Counties. Bucksport Marina is approximately 7 miles away on the Waccamaw River and Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway. The marina provides direct access to a tremendous stretch of navigable water and offers public boat ramps, docking, fuel, and other amenities for boaters and anglers. (Bucksport Marina)Approximately 8 miles away, Yauhannah Landing provides access to the Great Pee Dee River. Whether the day calls for fishing, boating, exploring the river or simply getting away from dry land for a few hours, having two major waterways within a short drive adds another dimension to this propertys location. The outdoor opportunities continue approximately 9 miles away at Waccamaw National Wildlife Refuge. Established in 1997, the refuge protects an impressive collection of blackwater and alluvial floodplain forests, tidal freshwater wetlands and historic rice-field habitats associated with the Waccamaw and Great Pee Dee Rivers.
